format: html

```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
library(dygraphs)
library(tidyquant)
library(timetk)
```

```{r}
stocks <- c("TSLA", "AAPL", "LMT", "AMZN","MSFT","WMT")

stock_prices <- tq_get(stocks) %>% 
    filter(date >= Sys.Date() - years(5))

View(stock_prices)
```

```{r}
stockxts <- stock_prices %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = symbol,
              values_from = close,
              id_cols = date) %>% 
  tk_xts(date = date)

View(stockxts)
```

```{r}
dygraph(stockxts) %>% 
  dyRangeSelector() %>% 
  dyAxis("y", label = "Stock price") %>% 
  dyLegend(show = "always") %>% 
   dyHighlight(highlightCircleSize = 5,
    highlightSeriesBackgroundAlpha = 0.3,
    hideOnMouseOut = FALSE)
  
```


Each one of my stocks is in an upward trend which would be very helpful and uplifting if I was actually investing in them. It seemed like tech industry stocks continuously went up with time and shopping centers like Walmart and Amazon went up as well but at a slower and less obvious pace.
